mechanism: C - cross-venue liquidation cascade propagation (Bybit leads, OKX lags), majors only
data_range: 2026-07-04 to 2026-08-29 (57 days, live derivatives_raw force_order feed) -- Binance has NO force_order feed at all (not in derivatives_raw) and its COIN-M liquidation backfill stops 2024-10-14, so Binance could not be included
unreliable_reason: 5-minute rolling liquidation notional is zero for >90-95% of windows on these symbols, so a percentile-based cascade threshold collapses to 0 (degenerate: 'cascade'==True on almost every minute), making the conditional test meaningless as designed. Needs a fixed-notional threshold and/or far longer history to fix.
interpretation: The EVENT-level propagation hypothesis is confirmed and strong for BTC/ETH (2-4x lift). But the originally-specced trade direction (follow/momentum-continuation) is wrong sign -- it loses money, significantly at 15-30min. The FADE (mean-reversion/overshoot-correction) direction is the right sign and marginally significant (t=2.5-2.9 at 15-30min) but gross edge (3.5-5.3bps) is close to or below realistic single-leg round-trip taker costs (~10bps) and only clears maker-level round-trip costs (~4bps) with little margin.
assumed_costs_bps: taker ~5bps one-way (10bps round trip) per exchange typical schedule; project's own stress config (configs/institutional/execution.yaml) uses taker_fee_bps=5.0, maker_fee_bps=2.0; more conservative scripts/run_parallel_50_*.py use taker_fee_bps=10 + slippage_bps=4
verdict: WEAK/PROMISING-BUT-MARGINAL - real propagation signal, but only marginally profitable after realistic costs, only proven for BTC/ETH, only 57 days of single-regime data, and the original directional hypothesis (follow) had to be inverted (fade) after testing
